content:
maya: Heads-up — we've been getting a bunch of transient ECC/Xid alerts from dcgm-exporter over the last 36h in us-west1. Lots of single-sample spikes that immediately recover and still fire pagerduty.

liam: Saw those too. Mostly single-card, low-count, and usually right after nightly kernel updates. Noise is drowning real issues. :face_with_raised_eyebrow: 

samir: Can you paste an example alert?

maya: Here's a stack of alerts from yesterday, simplified: 
- dcgm_ecc_singlebit_errors_total spike on gpu_id=gpu-3 instance=node-237
- dcgm_xid_errors_total incremented once, then nothing for hours

liam: My take: the current rule is firing on increase(...[1m]) >= 1 and routing straight to P0. We should aggregate and require sustained errors or multiple cards.

maya: Agree. Proposal: 1) Add a recording rule: 
```yaml
- record: gpu:dcgm_errors:increase_5m
  expr: increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) + increase(dcgm_ecc_singlebit_errors_total[5m])
```
2) Alert when sum by(instance) of that recording > 2 (i.e., >2 errors across GPUs on the node in 10m) or when a single gpu shows >=3 in 10m. That filters single-sample flutes.

natalie: Would we still catch a real degrading card early enough? I don't want to miss an actual flappy GPU.

samir: We can split severities: - warning for single / short spikes, - critical for sustained or multi-card. Also keep metrics for long-term regressions so optimize later.

liam: Example alert rule I hacked: 
```yaml
- alert: GPUNodeErrorBurst
  expr: sum by(instance)(increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[10m]) + increase(dcgm_ecc_singlebit_errors_total[10m])) > 2
  labels: { severity: warning, category: "gpu-health" }
  annotations: { runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-noise" }

- alert: GPUCardRepeatedErrors
  expr: increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[10m]) > 2
  labels: { severity: critical, category: "gpu-health" }
  annotations: { runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-card-triage" }
```
This makes single-sample increases go to warning channel and reduces PD churn.

oncall-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty integration will still escalate warnings if a human acknowledges? Check Alertmanager config for route -> pd severity mapping.

maya: Good point — we should also change Alertmanager route so warnings go to #gpu-warnings first (async triage) and only criticals go to oncall PDL.

taylor: Quick thinking — we should add a 'suppressed' label for alerts that meet known noisy signatures (e.g., kernel-driven spikes at 03:00). But be careful not to permanently silence.

liam: I implemented a recording rule that tags kernel-upgrade windows: 
```promql
kernel_update_window = time() - node_boot_time_seconds < 3600 and hour() == 3
```
Then we can add `and not kernel_update_window` to alerts during the experiment window.

natalie: That feels a bit heuristic, but fine as an experiment. Suggest: run in us-west1 (most noise), 48h experiment, collect alert counts and PD noise rate before/after.

maya: Proposed plan of action: 
1) Push recording rules + new alerts to staging, smoke test with synthetic metrics. (owner: liam)
2) Change Alertmanager routes to send 'warning' to #gpu-warnings and not PD. (owner: taylor)
3) Deploy to us-west1 Canary for 48h. Collect metrics: alert firing count, PD escalations, number of unique cards with >3 errors in 1h. (owner: natalie)
4) If PD noise drops >80% and we still catch critical degradations in historical replay, roll to prod.

liam: I'm on it. I'll open a PR with the rules and link test graphs.

samir: Add a note to the runbook to instruct on manual drain criteria: "If GPUCardRepeatedErrors critical fires -> cordon node, run dcgmi diag, if ECC/Xid persists, replace card."

taylor: I'll update routes. We'll keep a debug dashboard with per-card increase over 1h + logs.

natalie: If any of the criticals hit during the canary and look real, PD rules still apply — let's not be afraid to escalate.

maya: Cool. Thx all. Please ping in the thread when PRs are up and I'll validate the canary alerting window. :thumbsup: 

liam: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/-/merge_requests/432 (contains rule + recording + test graphs)

maya: Reviewing now.

oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall rota change tomorrow at 09:00 UTC — if an alert fires during handover, please follow escalation flow in runbook.

natalie: Experiment started at 1871234600 (canary). Will post results after 48h.

liam: Note for posterity: metric names used by dcgm-exporter are dcgm_xid_errors_total and dcgm_ecc_singlebit_errors_total (labels: instance, gpu_index, gpu_uuid). Use gpu_uuid for stable grouping.

maya: Perfect. Closing the loop after the canary.
